sentences.en: Today, we are talking about trauma bonds.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来谈谈“创伤联结”。

sentences.en: And no, not two people who bond through hardship because I hate to break it to you.
sentences.zh: 不，不是指两个人因为共同经历苦难而建立的友谊，因为我不想打破你的幻想，

sentences.en: That is actually not a trauma bond.
sentences.zh: 那其实并不是创伤联结。

sentences.en: We are talking about a powerful kind of connection that forms between two people when one person manipulates their own trauma or the trauma of the person that they are with
sentences.zh: 我们所说的是一种强大的联结，它形成于两个人之间，其中一方操纵自己的创伤或对方的创伤，

sentences.en: to create a highly dependent, highly painful, highly manipulative relationship that is founded on the highs and lows of emotional gaslighting, maybe even emotional abuse,
sentences.zh: 从而建立起一种高度依赖、极度痛苦且极具操纵性的关系，这种关系建立在情感煤气灯效应的起伏之中，甚至可能涉及情感虐待，

sentences.en: founded on hot and cold behavior, founded on betrayal and hurt rather than love.
sentences.zh: 建立在忽冷忽热的行为之上，建立在背叛和伤害而非爱之上。

sentences.en: What nobody tells you about trauma bonds is how often people who think they would never be susceptible to this kind of thing end up in these relationships all of the time
sentences.zh: 关于创伤联结，没人告诉你的是，那些认为自己绝不会陷入这种境地的人，却总是不断地陷入这种关系中，

sentences.en: because of how powerful inconsistency is at hijacking our brain's reward system.
sentences.zh: 这是因为“不一致性”在劫持我们大脑奖励系统方面有多么强大。

sentences.en: When somebody gives you the most perfect fantasy version of love one day and then switches it into the most terrible kind of love the next,
sentences.zh: 当某人今天给你最完美的梦幻般的爱，第二天却将其转变为最糟糕的对待时，

sentences.en: that emotional whiplash does something dangerous to your brain.
sentences.zh: 那种情感上的剧烈冲击会对你的大脑造成危险的影响。

sentences.en: It teaches you that if you just hold out a little bit longer, the good version is going to come back around.
sentences.zh: 它会让你觉得，只要再坚持一下，好的版本就会回来。

sentences.en: And so it leaves you holding on to potential and holding on to these terrible relationships and these terrible people because of the potential of reward.
sentences.zh: 于是，你因为对回报的期待，而紧紧抓住那些潜力和糟糕的关系，以及那些糟糕的人不放。

sentences.en: And that way, you know, this person, the person that people form a trauma bond with becomes both their biggest source of unhappiness,
sentences.zh: 就这样，你知道，这个人——那个与人形成创伤联结的人——既成了他们最大的痛苦来源，

sentences.en: but also their biggest source of happiness at times because this person is the one who can give and take those things, who can give and take safety.
sentences.zh: 但有时也成了他们最大的快乐来源，因为这个人是唯一能给予和剥夺这些东西、给予和剥夺安全感的人。

sentences.en: People who have never experienced this may look at it from the outside and think, I don't know, why don't you just leave?
sentences.zh: 从未经历过的人可能会从旁观者的角度想：我不知道，你为什么不直接离开呢？

sentences.en: That person's obviously not good for you.
sentences.zh: 那个人显然对你不好。

sentences.en: Why don't you know you deserve better?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不知道你值得更好的？

sentences.en: Why don't you just walk away?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接走开呢？

sentences.en: But what they don't understand is the insanely powerful neurobiological, psychological, physical, emotionally addictive patterns that this kind of relationship creates,
sentences.zh: 但他们不明白的是，这种关系所产生的神经生物学、心理学、生理学和情感上的成瘾模式是多么强大，

sentences.en: which essentially mean that our own self-preservation, our own instincts, our own emotions, our rationality, it all just gets so totally scrambled.
sentences.zh: 这本质上意味着我们自身的自我保护、本能、情绪和理性，全都变得彻底混乱了。

sentences.en: I think what they don't realize is how smart abusers and partners can be, how well they understand the mechanisms of insecurity and psychology
sentences.zh: 我认为他们没有意识到虐待者和伴侣可以有多聪明，他们有多了解不安全感和心理学的机制，

sentences.en: and how well they can manipulate love.
sentences.zh: 以及他们能多好地操纵爱。

sentences.en: So this is exactly what we're going to be revealing and talking about today.
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是我们今天要揭示和讨论的内容。

sentences.en: If you have ever found yourself in this kind of trauma bond, if you are recovering and healing from a relationship that matches this pattern,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经发现自己处于这种创伤联结中，如果你正在从一段符合这种模式的关系中恢复和疗愈，

sentences.en: or if you're just watching like a friend or anybody in your life going through this and you're trying to understand like how you can help them,
sentences.zh: 或者如果你只是在看着朋友或生活中的某个人经历这一切，并试图了解如何帮助他们，

sentences.en: I think and I hope that this episode will bring you some clarity.
sentences.zh: 我想，也希望这一集能为你带来一些清晰的认识。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology of trauma bonds.
sentences.zh: 那么，废话不多说，让我们进入创伤联结的心理学。

sentences.en: Let's start by really clarifying because this is totally essential.
sentences.zh: 让我们先澄清一下，因为这绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: We really need to clarify what we mean by a trauma bond because it has been used very, very casually these days and that has definitely diluted its meaning considerably,
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要明确“创伤联结”的含义，因为它现在被用得非常非常随意，这无疑大大稀释了它的意义，

sentences.en: not because of anybody's poor intentions, just because of concept creep.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为谁的意图不好，只是因为“概念蔓延”。

sentences.en: Concept creep is essentially the casual expansion of serious terms to mean less and less serious things and therefore take away the important meaning of these words.
sentences.zh: 概念蔓延本质上是指严肃术语被随意扩大，用来指代越来越不严肃的事情，从而剥夺了这些词汇原本重要的含义。

sentences.en: I think we have all heard of people who have become friends at a terrible workplace, you know, joke that they are trauma bonded
sentences.zh: 我想我们都听说过在糟糕的工作场所成为朋友的人开玩笑说他们是“创伤联结”，

sentences.en: or people who have dealt with like the same tragic, awful ex will be like, how'd you guys meet?
sentences.zh: 或者处理过同样悲惨、糟糕的前任的人会说：你们是怎么认识的？

sentences.en: Oh, we like, we have like a trauma bond.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们有种创伤联结。

sentences.en: We're like trauma bonded.
sentences.zh: 我们算是创伤联结了。

sentences.en: That is very different to the original meaning of this term.
sentences.zh: 这与该术语的原始含义大不相同。

sentences.en: Trauma bonding was first devised in 1997 by this man called Dr. Patrick Karnes, who interestingly also is known for his work actually on sex addiction as a sidebar,
sentences.zh: 创伤联结最早由Patrick Karnes博士在1997年提出，有趣的是，他作为副业也以研究性成瘾而闻名，

sentences.en: but he essentially created, discovered, founded this term to refer to a relationship between an abuser and an abused person or a manipulative person
sentences.zh: 但他本质上创造、发现并确立了这个术语，用来指代虐待者与被虐待者之间，或操纵者与目标之间的一种关系，

sentences.en: and a target that is formed in a way that gets somebody to stay against their best interests because of trauma, because trauma creates a bond.
sentences.zh: 这种关系的形成方式让某人违背自己的最佳利益而留下来，因为创伤，因为创伤创造了一种联结。

sentences.en: In contrast to like the normal use of the word bond to describe like a deep, healthy reaction to love and emotional vulnerability and connection,
sentences.zh: 与“联结”一词通常用来描述对爱、情感脆弱和连接的深层健康反应不同，

sentences.en: trauma bonding refers to how we respond to emotional volatility and how we respond to control.
sentences.zh: 创伤联结指的是我们如何应对情感波动以及如何应对控制。

sentences.en: Sometimes, you know, actually tunneling further into the relationship that is creating these bad feelings for protection when it's obviously against our best interests
sentences.zh: 有时，你知道，实际上为了寻求保护而进一步深入到那种制造负面情绪的关系中，尽管这显然违背了我们的最佳利益，

sentences.en: because for some reason our brain isn't able to rationally respond in these situations.
sentences.zh: 因为出于某种原因，我们的大脑在这些情况下无法做出理性的反应。

sentences.en: It has been scrambled by somebody else's behavior.
sentences.zh: 它已经被别人的行为搞乱了。

sentences.en: A bond is, you know, in simpler terms, really just a connection.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，联结其实就是一种连接。

sentences.en: A trauma bond is a connection that is forged through something sinister, but it is a connection nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 创伤联结是一种通过某种险恶事物锻造出来的连接，但它终究是一种连接。

sentences.en: In short, it is an attachment based on cycles of threat and relief, which leave the person in this relationship desperate for approval.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这是一种基于威胁与解脱循环的依恋，使处于这种关系中的人极度渴望得到认可。

sentences.en: This can happen, yes, most often with a romantic partner, but it can also happen with a parent, can happen with a friend, it can happen
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实最常发生在浪漫伴侣之间，但也可能发生在父母、朋友之间，可能发生在

sentences.en: with an institution, a mentor, anybody who has emotional control and can take what somebody needs from a relationship and exploit it, these have the capacity
sentences.zh: 机构、导师之间，任何拥有情感控制权并能利用某人对关系的需要的人，都有可能

sentences.en: to turn into trauma bonds.
sentences.zh: 将其转化为创伤联结。

sentences.en: The way that a trauma bond begins is often through intense affection and praise from the abuser, love bombing, like major declarations of love, what appears to be fierce devotion.
sentences.zh: 创伤联结的开始通常源于虐待者强烈的爱意和赞美，即“爱之轰炸”，比如重大的爱的宣言，看起来像是炽热的忠诚。

sentences.en: It's like a huge emotional high, it's super intense.
sentences.zh: 这就像一种巨大的情感高潮，非常强烈。

sentences.en: It's like, it's a magnetic, addictive feeling to be cared for in such a way.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式被关怀，是一种具有磁性的、令人上瘾的感觉。

sentences.en: They may also, and this is critical, tell the person that they are intending to form a trauma bond with stories of their own trauma, particularly from their childhood,
sentences.zh: 他们可能还会——这一点至关重要——告诉那个他们打算建立创伤联结的人，关于他们自己创伤的故事，特别是童年时期的，

sentences.en: particularly from past relationships, to generate like a deep psychological hold over this other person, but also to elicit sympathy.
sentences.zh: 特别是过去关系中的，以此对另一个人产生深层的心理控制，同时也为了博取同情。

sentences.en: This stage is essential.
sentences.zh: 这个阶段是必不可少的。

sentences.en: It basically provides this abuser, this person, with an emotional alibi for their future bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 它基本上为这个虐待者、这个人，提供了未来不良行为的情感不在场证明。

sentences.en: And they need to do this in order to engage the next part of their plan, because eventually like their behavior is going to switch.
sentences.zh: 他们需要这样做来实施计划的下一部分，因为最终他们的行为会发生转变。

sentences.en: They're going to become cruel.
sentences.zh: 他们会变得残忍。

sentences.en: And having this reason why they do it to fall back on helps them dismiss their behavior to you.
sentences.zh: 而拥有这个他们之所以这样做的理由作为后盾，有助于他们向你推卸自己的行为。

sentences.en: Again, like I said, eventually it's going to escalate.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，正如我所说，最终情况会升级。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that this escalation is often also randomly juxtaposed with warmth and affection.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，这种升级往往也随机地与温暖和爱意并置。

sentences.en: It will be like, I love you.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我爱你。

sentences.en: You've disappointed me like nobody ever has.
sentences.zh: 你让我失望得前所未有。

sentences.en: You're the greatest thing that's ever happened to me.
sentences.zh: 你是我遇到过最棒的事。

sentences.en: I never want to see you again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不想见到你了。

sentences.en: I think you're beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你很美。

sentences.en: You disgust me.
sentences.zh: 你让我感到恶心。

sentences.en: This flip-flop, flip-flop.
sentences.zh: 这种反反复复，翻来覆去。

sentences.en: In his article, Love and Stockholm Syndrome,
sentences.zh: 在他的文章《爱与斯德哥尔摩综合征：爱上虐待者的谜团》中，心理学家Joseph Carver博士称之为“小恩小惠感知”。

sentences.en: The Mystery of Loving an Abuser, this psychologist, Dr. Joseph Carver, he calls this small kindness perception.
sentences.zh: 也许虐待者一直对某人进行冷暴力，然后他们通过礼物或拥抱打破冷暴力，以此展示小恩小惠。

sentences.en: Perhaps the abuser has been giving somebody the silent treatment, and then they show them the small kindness by breaking the silent treatment with a gift or a hug.
sentences.zh: 也许他们会排斥你、忽视你，然后突然转过身来想要你在身边。

sentences.en: Maybe they will exclude you, ignore you, and then suddenly turn around and want you around.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种解脱、痛苦与解脱的循环，解脱、痛苦、痛苦与解脱，就像不知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: This is that cycle of relief, pain and relief, relief, pain, pain and relief, like not knowing which one's going to come.
sentences.zh: 同样，他们既成了恐惧的来源，也成了安全感的来源，这意味着即使某人想要离开，他们所有的情绪调节，

sentences.en: Again, they become an equal source of fear, but also of safety, meaning that even if somebody wants to walk away, all of their emotional regulation,
sentences.zh: 好的和坏的，都与另一个人捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: good and bad, is tied up to this other person.
sentences.zh: 有足够多的好日子来诱惑你，足够多的坏日子来困惑你，还有足够多的借口让他们给你，让你以为他们可以改变。

sentences.en: There are enough good days to entice you and enough bad days to confuse you, and enough excuses that they're giving you to think that they can change.
sentences.zh: 这种忽冷忽热的人格被描述为“双面灵魂伴侣”，我认为这是一个描述这种情况的绝妙术语。

sentences.en: This hot and cold personality has been described essentially like a two-faced soulmate, which I think is like a brilliant term for describing this.
sentences.zh: 它基本上符合这种亲密与强化、奖励与惩罚的模式。

sentences.en: It basically fits this pattern of intimate and reinforcement and reward and punishment.
sentences.zh: 它符合这种模式，即这个人是一个身体里的两个不同的人，而这两个不同的人很难拆解，因为好的时候真的太好了，

sentences.en: It fits this pattern of like, this person is two different people in one body, and these two different people are so difficult to disentangle because the good is just so good,
sentences.zh: 而坏的时候又与之截然不同，以至于根本无法分辨什么是真，什么是假。

sentences.en: and the bad is so different to that, that it's literally impossible to know what's real and what's not.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，这种爱意与残忍的循环往往会持续数年，对某些人来说甚至是一辈子，这说起来真是悲剧。

sentences.en: From there, the cycle of affection and cruelty continues, often for years, sometimes even for a lifetime for some people, which is tragic to say.
sentences.zh: 那么，它为什么会发生呢？

sentences.en: So why does it happen in the first place?
sentences.zh: 有哪些警示信号？
